title: Checked access
description:
Turn the preconditions of `std::vector` members into checks.

```
checked(v)[2] = 30
checked(v)[9] -> precondition failed: index 9 < size 3
checked(empty).front() -> precondition failed: not empty
```
hints: The page for `front` says "Calling front on an empty container causes undefined behavior" (lesson 1.04).
Many standard libraries have a debug mode that checks these for you (`_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS`, MSVC's debug iterators).
requirements: A small wrapper `Checked<T>` around a `std::vector<T>&` with `operator[]`, `front`, `back` and `pop_back`.
Each checks the precondition from its reference page and throws `std::logic_error` with a clear message.
Show which members already check for you (`at`) and which do not.
stretch: Do the same for `std::string::substr`, which does check, and say what it throws.
